newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean gold output seen at 80,000 kg in 2000.
newsitem.headline: Chilean gold output seen at 80,000 kg in 2000.

text.p: Chile will be at least the world's 10th largest producer of gold in the year 2000, with annual production climbing to up to 80,000 kg from about 55,000 kg currently, Mining Minister Benjamin Teplizky said.
Gold production in Chile, where copper is king, has been rising steadily due to large new strikes by Bema Gold Corp and Barrick, and a plethora of smaller producers, said Teplizky.

''Chile is becoming a major gold producer. Production will be on the order of 75,000 to 80,000 kilos in the year 2000 but it's not exactly clear yet because they keep finding new deposits,'' he told reporters for foreign media.

''By way of example, they're now saying Cerro Casale is even larger than Refugio,'' he said, referring to two Bema deposits. Bema has reported 24.8 million ounces of gold reserves at Cerro Casale alone.
Chilean gold output this year will be 54,000 to 55,000 kg, up from about 35,000 to 40,000 kg early in the 1990s, Teplizky said.

He reiterated official forecasts of copper production this year of 3.4 million to 3.5 million tonnes, rising to about 4.5 million tonnes in the year 2000, or about 40 percent of world production by then.
